name: Shift report 2026-11-18 08:44 UTC — QA gate hardening, increment M1 not reachable yet
description:
#TL; DR;
**Status: AT RISK.** The QA gate of this project (codx-docs) still cannot judge a single change, because it is asked to run a test suite and the project has never declared one. Everything else in this shift was re-organisation, not progress. Two items need a human: the `qa_policy` declaration cannot be applied by the agent, and 45 pending files sit unapproved since a previous change. Nothing is blocked on customers or on any external party.

## 1. Summary
Goal of this workstream: make the QA gate of the `codx-docs` project produce a meaningful verdict (pass / fail / approve) instead of failing for a reason unrelated to the change under review. Business outcome: doc deliveries stop being blocked or waved through by an unreliable gate.
This shift: closed the two cards whose acceptance was already met, reframed one card that was a management decision in disguise, re-dated the blocked card to a date the team can actually meet, and created the sprint that holds the work.

## 2. Scope
**In scope this increment (M1–M3):** decision on the project root · `qa_policy` schema check + docs suite declaration · `tests.no-suite` cleared so the gate can run.
**Out of scope (M4, deferred):** host provisioning of a working PDF engine (`c2dc4ded`, due 2026-12-01, low) — no customer-facing impact, the limitation is documented in `docs/delivery-contract.md`.

## 3. Increment plan — sprint `QA gate hardening (18-21 Nov 2026)`
| M | Deliverable | Owner | Date | Deployable? | Demoable? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | QA gate root decided (docs/ as project root = option C) + recorded in `delivery-contract.md` | ProjectManager | 2026-11-18 | yes | yes — the contract text is the artefact | **Done** (`b776e9a7`) |
| M2 | `qa_policy` schema verified; docs suite (`docs:build` = `vitepress build`) declared in `.codx/project.json` | software_developer | 2026-11-20 | yes | yes — paste `qa_plan()` + `qa_run_tests()` output | **On hold** (`e684ce5c`), wake 2026-11-20 08:00 — *critical path* |
| M3 | `tests.no-suite` (HIGH) cleared; gate returns a real verdict | software_developer | 2026-11-21 | yes | yes — gate output on a real change | **On hold** (`3fb379ae`), wake 2026-11-20 09:00 |
| M4 | Platform repo (`api/` + `client/`) gating decision if option C stands | management + software_developer | decision by 2026-11-20 | n/a | yes — one-screen options | **On hold** (`42c8d580`), wake 2026-11-20 10:00 |
| M5 | Host PDF engine (optional) | software_developer | 2026-12-01 | n/a | no — internal tooling | **On hold**, low (`c2dc4ded`), wake 2026-11-25 08:00 |

## 4. Dependencies & critical path
`M2 (qa_policy + suite declared)` → `M3 (gate runs, no-suite gone)` → `a8be6182 (approval verdict is meaningful)` → M4 decision.
M1 is done and unblocks M2. M5 is off the critical path entirely.
M4 is a decision, not work: it can be answered in parallel with M2/M3 and must be before the platform repo is assumed gated.

## 5. Risks
| Risk | Impact | Prob. | Mitigation | Owner | Needs decision? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The agent cannot write `.codx/project.json` (`qa_policy`) | gate stays red; M3 slips indefinitely | medium | `e684ce5c` carries the exact JSON block and the escalation; human applies it in one step | ProjectManager | **yes** |
| `docs:build` (vitepress) is a build, not a test suite — a "green" gate would be a false positive | management trusts a gate that proves nothing | medium | M3 acceptance requires showing what the suite actually asserts; if it only builds, add a real check in the same card | software_developer | yes |
| 45 files pending approval in `a8be6182` since a previous change | the gate is not trusted; approvals pile up | high | due 2026-11-19: approve or reject explicitly, do not let it roll | management | **yes** |
| Option C leaves `api/` + `client/` ungated | regressions reach the platform repo undetected | medium | M4 decision card, due 2026-11-20 | management | **yes** |

## 6. Decisions needed from management
1. **Apply the `qa_policy` declaration** (blocker, decide by **2026-11-20**). Options: (a) a human pastes the JSON from `e684ce5c` into `.codx/project.json` — *recommended, 2 minutes, no code risk*; (b) grant a profile with write access to the control plane and let the agent do it — slower, needs a permission change. **Recommendation: (a).**
2. **Approve or reject the 45 pending files** in `a8be6182` (decide by **2026-11-19**). Recommendation: approve the substantive change (`delivery-contract.md`) and reject the `.codx` control-plane noise.
3. **Platform repo gating** in `42c8d580` (decide by **2026-11-20**). Recommendation: keep option C for this project and open a separate gating card on the parent repo — one gate per repository is the only configuration that stays truthful.

## 7. Next demo & checkpoint
**Next checkpoint: 2026-11-20, 08:00 UTC (wake of `e684ce5c`).**
Management will see: `qa_plan()` and `qa_run_tests()` output on this repo, and the gate's verdict on a deliberately broken change (one line removed) to prove it can fail.
Needed to run it: the `qa_policy` declaration applied (decision 1).

## 8. Demo script (once M2 lands)
1. Open `.codx/project.json`, show the `qa_policy.suites` entry.
2. Run the gate on the clean tree → expect pass.
3. Remove one line from a doc, run the gate → expect **fail** with a specific reason.
4. Restore the line, re-run → pass. (≈3 minutes.)
Question for management: is "build succeeds" enough, or should the suite assert links and version consistency too?

## Board state after this shift
Sprint `QA gate hardening (18-21 Nov 2026)` holds all six cards. `Done`: `b776e9a7`, `755647b0`. `Scheduled/onhold` with wakes: `e684ce5c` (20 Nov 08:00), `3fb379ae` (20 Nov 09:00), `42c8d580` (20 Nov 10:00), `c2dc4ded` (25 Nov 08:00). `Working/onhold`: `a8be6182` (due 19 Nov, wake 19 Nov 08:00).

## Addendum 2026-11-18 08:48 UTC — escalation lane used, report corrected

The report above said the two human blockers were "scheduled". That was imprecise and has been fixed on the board:

| Card | Was | Now | Wake (unchanged) | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `e684ce5c` qa_policy declaration | `Scheduled` / onhold | **`User action needed`** / onhold · progress 60 | 2026-11-20 08:00 | high (raised) |
| `a8be6182` approval of 45 files | `Working` / onhold | **`User action needed`** / onhold | 2026-11-19 08:00 | high (raised) |

**Why:** each of them cannot advance without a human — one because the agent has no write path to `.codx/project.json` (all routes tried and recorded on the card), the other because it is an approve/reject decision. Keeping them among scheduled AI work hid the only two things management actually has to do.

Not moved, deliberately: `42c8d580` (platform-repo gating) is a decision I *prepare* and present at the 20 Nov checkpoint, so it stays `Scheduled`; `3fb379ae` is real work for `software_developer` once the policy lands; `c2dc4ded` is low-priority host provisioning with no milestone behind it.

Escalation lane used: **2 of 5 open cards.** If that number grows next shift, the increment is not moving — the number itself is the health indicator.
